about: The Market Board's data (Docs/Design/79-a-staged-economy.md, 5 and 7; Core/RatwMarket.cpp). `groups`: each good's depth group and its depthBase (a market's depth for a good is max(20, depthBase x catchment^0.6) x depthScale). A good's group is its entry in `goods`, else its catalogue category's in `categories`, else `fallback`. `district`: a static price factor by a keeper's quarter (its voice table's `quarter`), by group or `all`, inside the clamp. `times`: the slider's narrow move on staples and luxuries (D2), at hard, lean, ordinary, good and boom. `seasonSpanMost`: a season group's price swing (its dearest season over its cheapest) is rescaled to at most this, so it fits the clamp with room for pressure (the user, 2026-11-08: at a season's ends, with the region factors, players' pressure always keeps at least x1.10 up and x0.90 down inside the clamp, for every good; 1.06 leaves x1.136 up and x0.893 down; market_tests' seasonsLeavePressureRoom pins it). `region`: dearer where a good isn't made. `buys`: what a kind of shop also buys from players in the staged economy (D5: the smithy, the ironworks and the foundry buy iron ore). `shelves`: a ware's shelf where it isn't the starting stock (4, swords 3; moved from city_loop.json: theriac, the apothecary's rare cure-all, one at a time). `seasons`: the seven season groups (moved from city_loop.json, gone since doc 79's Phase 3): each group's goods and, for Spring, Summer, Autumn and Winter (each the value at the season's middle day, the days between blended), in percent of normal, its `price` (rescaled to fit the clamp) and its `shelf` (how full the shops keep it). A world's own season records (the DM's Economy tab) still lay their price and shelf over a group's. The clamp's ends (0.80, 1.28), the sell share (0.55) and the backstop (0.95) are constants, never data. `rules` (Core's Rules[] defaults), and `services`, `luxuries`, `houseBusinesses`, `estates` and `wharf`, kept from the city's loop in Phase 3 for the phases that will read them (each `about` names its phase; nothing in Core reads those five yet).

rules.about: The rules' defaults (doc 79, 12; Core/RatwItems.h Rules[] names them, with their ranges): the clamps (neverHungry, neverBroke), the days of food more before a Restday or festival (buyAheadDays), the Board's pressure settings, and staged trade's (Phase 4): the wagons' frequency in percent (caravanRate), the most wagons and farm carts on the roads at once (wagonsOnRoad, cartsOnRoad), a bandit camp's most strength (campStrengthMost) and a bounty's most pennies (bountyMost); and the port's (Phase 5): the ships a week at a port (shipsPerWeek: 0 none, even with a port; its own 2 gives 1-3 a week by the slider and the season, a week running one either side of the rule and fewer in winter); and street life's (Phase 6): the most thefts a market sees in a day (theftCap) and whether a household's shopping is a member walking to the counter where a player is near (errandRunners: 1 on, D21; off, the household's food waits for the player to leave); and staged events' (Phase 7): the events a market sees in percent of the `events` block's own (eventRate: 0 none, 100 the list's 1-3 a week, 300 three times as many) and whether the DM's Times nudges and harvest overrides post a notice on the boards (overrideNotices: 1 on). A world's own `rule` records (live.economy.rules) are over these; a name not here or in Rules[] is skipped.

services.about: The city's services (doc 79, 6.5 and 12: kept, at a frequency by band): each a catalogue item (category service) a business does, about once every `every` days a household, `for: patrons` a patron's. Since Phase 6 (street life) they are staged sales: each household has each done about once every `every` days times its band's `services` (status.json; a patron's only for the rich, and for the poor only those marked `poor: true`, the barber's: 6.5's "a barber rarely"), at a business of its kind in its market; nothing is paid or kept, and each counts toward that business's trade against its ordinary trade (the `business` fact). A world's `service` record (the Rules panel) turns one off or changes its every.

luxuries.about: The luxuries (doc 72, Phase 5: cheese, a comic luxury for wolves): the goods the rich buy. The Board's `times` swings their depth group (luxury, by `goods` and `categories` above); since Phase 6 (street life) the rich and the comfortable buy them from the shelves of the shops that set them out (status.json's `luxury`, a chance a week), and Phase 8 (talk) reads it for their boasts and complaints.

houseBusinesses.about: The Houses' businesses in the city (doc 72): a business at one of these buildings is its House's. No money moves by it, and nothing in Core reads it yet: the bands find the Houses' people by `houses()` today; Phase 8 (talk) reads this list for who owns what.

estates.about: The Houses' estates (doc 72, Phase 6): each House's people by the words of their posts. No purse (the estates' money went with the city's loop), and nothing in Core reads it: the guarantees (doc 79, 6.3) go by district (the Heights and the estates) since Phase 2. Kept for Phase 8 (talk: a House's people); Phase 9 drops it if talk doesn't take it.

list.name: House Grayrock's estate (the wharf and the sea trade)

wharf.about: The port (doc 79, 8.3; Phase 5 and its repair; goods from doc 73's lists). `posts`: the words in a post's title that make its market a port (its harbourmaster and Wharf office, the hands unloading ships, the cranes; never the bare word wharf, which a tannery or a smokehouse by the water has in its name, so Ridgemere's overseer of the Grayrock wharf is listed by his own words; the sea trade's other posts there, its carriers and store keepers, are the port's too, but make no port alone). `never`: goods no ship brings (cheese: the user's). `imports`: the ships' own goods; at a port's market those its shops set out and its workshops don't make wait for a ship (D27), and so does whatever else its shops set out that nothing in the realm makes and no wagon or cart brings. `takes`: what ships take away, of what its shops sell, buy or make. `ships`: the ships' names (letters and spaces; each passes the forbidden-word check, in Core's loader too). `cargoWords`: a good's words in a cargo where the catalogue's name won't do (a thing counted by the piece is put in the plural by rule: World::cargoWords). Core reads them (market::Data's wharfPosts, shipNever, shipBrings, shipTakes, shipNames, cargoWords; World's RatwPort.cpp): a world with no port uses none of it. Atlas's Wharf panel shows the goods until Phase 9 retargets it.

events.about: Staged events and the slider's causes (doc 79, 8.4, 8.5 and D25; Phase 7; Core/RatwEvents.cpp). Each market sees `perWeek` events a week, one more or fewer by a seeded score (1-3 at 2), times the rule eventRate, each of `list` it can show, rolled a week ahead and kept on the Market Board (a restart shows the same; a host's edit here changes none already rolled). An entry: `id` (a-z, 0-9 and _; never the forbidden word, as letters anywhere), `words` (its cause, said in talk, the price list's tooltip and the Times' cause), `notice` (on its market's board, signed `sign`), `cry` (the crier's line at the square), with {market}, {day}, {goods}, {ship} and {from} filled ({Market}: capitalised); `goods`: each good's pressure the event presses toward (within 0.3 either way: inside the clamp), only those its market's shops sell or buy, four at most; `days` it presses (1-7), `times` its points on its market's Times while it does (within 20), `ahead` the days its notice is up before it (0: it is posted as it begins), `hour`, `weight` (how often it is picked), `needs` (city: the realm's largest market; port; cart: a staffed farm's cart to the market, `yields` the pressure on what that cart brings, `holdsCart` the cart kept home that day; festival: the day before a festival), `ship` (docks: it comes in with a ship of the port's timetable, `brings` the pressure on that ship's cargo, cancelled if the ship never comes; lost: the ship is lost at sea), `refill` (its cheap goods set out as it begins), `crowd` (a crowd at its market's place or the Wharf while on). A bad entry is left out, the rest kept; every text is checked for the forbidden word (whole words), and so is a Dungeon Master's cause. `causes`: the words a move of the prosperity slider comes with when the DM writes none (`down`, `up`: `words`, `notice`, `cry`), and the notice and cry for one the DM writes ({cause}, {Cause}). Events never touch money, bands or posts.

list.notice: A House wedding in {market} on {day}. The stewards are buying {goods}.
list.cry: Hear ye! A House wedding on {day}, and wine for the stewards!

list.notice: Fire at the works in {market}! {Goods} dear till it is put to rights.
list.cry: Fire at the works! Hands wanted with buckets!

list.notice: A good catch is in at {market}: {goods} cheap a day or two.
list.cry: Fresh fish! A good catch in!

list.notice: Blight in the orchards: {goods} dear at {market} this week.

list.words: the buying ahead for the festival
list.notice: The festival is near: the inns and kitchens of {market} are buying {goods}.
list.cry: The festival is near! Inns and kitchens buying!

list.words: a lame ox on the cart from {from}
list.notice: The cart from {from} is not coming today: a lame ox. {Goods} short at {market} till it does.
{Ship} is due on {day} with a rich cargo: {goods} cheap at the Wharf when she is in.
list.cry: {Ship} is in, and a rich cargo with her!

list.notice: {Ship} is lost at sea with all her cargo. {Goods} dear at {market} till another comes.
list.cry: {Ship} is lost! Prayers at the chapel for her crew!

list.notice: The mill wheel is stopped for mending: {goods} dear in {market} till it turns again.

list.words: the drovers in with their herds
list.notice: The drovers are in at {market} with their herds: {goods} cheap a day or two.
The salt pans are flooded: {goods} dear in {market} this week.
The brewers have brewed too much: {goods} cheap at {market}.

down.notice: By order of the Crown: a levy for the war, on every household and trade.
down.cry: Hear ye! The Crown levies for the war!

down.notice: Rot in the realm's granaries: bread and grain will be dear this season.
down.cry: Hear ye! Rot in the granaries!

down.notice: A hard winter coming: the roads slow, the stores thin.
down.cry: Hear ye! A hard winter is on us!

up.words: the silver strike in the hills
up.notice: Silver struck in the hills: coin and work for all who want it.
up.cry: Hear ye! Silver in the hills!

up.notice: Peace is sealed with the north: the roads are open and trade comes back.
up.cry: Hear ye! Peace with the north!

up.notice: The richest harvest in years is coming in: full barns and full purses.
